# Standard Normal Distribution Table

For a standard normal random variable, $Z$, the mean is 0 and the standard deviation is 1. Each entry in the table gives the area under the standard normal curve **between the mean, $z=0$, and the listed positive z-score**:

$$
A=P(0<Z<z)
$$

The table does not directly report cumulative probability from negative infinity. Use symmetry and the rules below to obtain lower- and upper-tail probabilities.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-standard-normal
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "Areas between the mean and selected positive z-scores."

library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

z_values <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 3.00, by = 0.05), 1.64, 1.96, 2.58)))
areas <- pnorm(z_values) - 0.5

pairs_per_row <- 3
rows <- ceiling(length(z_values) / pairs_per_row)
pad <- rows * pairs_per_row - length(z_values)

if (pad > 0) {
  z_values <- c(z_values, rep(NA_real_, pad))
  areas <- c(areas, rep(NA_real_, pad))
}

z_matrix <- matrix(z_values, nrow = rows, ncol = pairs_per_row)
area_matrix <- matrix(areas, nrow = rows, ncol = pairs_per_row)

format_z <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf("%.2f", x))
format_area <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf("%.4f", x))

normal_table <- data.frame(
  z1 = format_z(z_matrix[, 1]),
  area1 = format_area(area_matrix[, 1]),
  z2 = format_z(z_matrix[, 2]),
  area2 = format_area(area_matrix[, 2]),
  z3 = format_z(z_matrix[, 3]),
  area3 = format_area(area_matrix[, 3]),
  check.names = FALSE
)

normal_output <- kable(
  normal_table,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = "cccccc",
  col.names = c("z", "Area", "z", "Area", "z", "Area")
)

if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  normal_output <- kable_styling(
    normal_output,
    latex_options = "hold_position",
    font_size = 9
  )
} else {
  normal_output <- kable_styling(normal_output, full_width = FALSE)
}

normal_output
```

## Using the Table

Let $A$ represent the area obtained from the table for the absolute value of the z-score.

| Desired probability | Calculation |
|:--------------------|:------------|
| $P(Z<z)$ when $z>0$ | $0.5+A$ |
| $P(Z>z)$ when $z>0$ | $0.5-A$ |
| $P(Z<z)$ when $z<0$ | $0.5-A$ |
| $P(Z>z)$ when $z<0$ | $0.5+A$ |

::: {.callout-tip title="Negative z-scores"}
The normal distribution is symmetric. Look up the absolute value of a negative z-score and then select the appropriate rule from the table above.
:::

## Worked Example: $z=1.25$

The table reports an area of $A=0.3944$ between 0 and 1.25. Therefore:

$$
P(Z<1.25)=0.5+0.3944=0.8944
$$

$$
P(Z>1.25)=0.5-0.3944=0.1056
$$

By symmetry:

$$
P(Z<-1.25)=0.1056
$$

```{r}
#| label: fig-standard-normal-example
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Area between the mean and z = 1.25."
#| fig-alt: "Standard normal curve with the area between zero and 1.25 shaded."
#| fig-height: 2.6
#| fig-width: 6

library(ggplot2)

example_z <- 1.25
curve_data <- data.frame(z = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 1200))
curve_data$density <- dnorm(curve_data$z)
shaded_data <- subset(curve_data, z >= 0 & z <= example_z)

ggplot(curve_data, aes(x = z, y = density)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_area(
    data = shaded_data,
    fill = "grey65",
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0, example_z), linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.63, y = 0.13, label = "Area = 0.3944") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 1.25, 2, 3)) +
  labs(x = "z-score", y = "Density") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
```

If a calculated z-score falls between table entries, use the closest listed value unless instructed to interpolate. A z-score beyond the table represents a very small tail probability; report that it lies beyond the table rather than treating its probability as zero.
